title: Fluency: the slope is covariance over variance

families.skill: the least squares slope from the sums
families.prompt: Paired data have $S_{{xy}} = {sxy}$, $S_{{xx}} = {sxx}$ and $S_{{yy}} = {syy}$. What is the least squares slope $b$ of $y$ on $x$?

wrong.line: You divided $S_{{xx}}$ by $S_{{xy}}$. The slope is $S_{{xy}}/S_{{xx}}$: covariance over the variance of $x$.
You divided by $S_{{yy}}$, which gives the slope of $x$ on $y$. For $y$ on $x$, divide by $S_{{xx}}$.

families.skill: the intercept from the slope and the means
families.prompt: A least squares line has slope $b = {b}$, and the data have $\bar x = {xb}$ and $\bar y = {yb}$. What is the intercept $a$?

wrong.line: You added $b\bar x$. The line passes through $(\bar x, \bar y)$, so $a = \bar y - b\bar x$.
You swapped the means. The intercept is $\bar y - b\bar x$, with $\bar y = {yb}$.

solution: The line passes through $(\bar x, \bar y)$, so $a = \bar y - b\bar x$.

families.skill: the slope from a correlation and two sds
families.prompt: A {ys}'s daily returns have correlation {r} with the {xs}'s. The {xs}'s daily sd is {sx}% and the {ys}'s is {sy}%. What is the slope of the {ys}'s return on the {xs}'s, to 3 decimal places?

wrong.line: You used $r\,s_x/s_y$. The slope of $y$ on $x$ is $r\,s_y/s_x$: the {ys}'s sd on top.
That is $s_y/s_x$ alone. Multiply by the correlation, {r}.
